standard_prerequisites.name: The class of the diagonal and the minimal number of pure tensors
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma on the pairings of the Kunneth components of the class of the diagonal, implying that the class cannot be written as a sum of fewer pure tensors than the sum of the Betti numbers
standard_prerequisites.use: Bounds the total dimension of the cohomology of the projective line by two.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nonvanishing of the degree zero cohomology and Poincare duality
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma that the degree zero cohomology of a nonempty scheme is nonzero, and axiom (A)(b) on the perfect pairing between complementary degrees
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the dimension in degree zero is nonzero and equals the dimension in the top degree, which pins down the two remaining dimensions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Compatibility of the cycle class map with pullbacks
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Axiom (C)(a) on the compatibility of the cycle class map with pullbacks, together with additivity of the cycle class map under addition of cycles
standard_prerequisites.use: Computes the class of the diagonal of the product of the projective line with itself from the classes of the two rulings.

core_obligations: Compute the class of the diagonal (proof lines 2905-2913): for a rational point the diagonal of the product of the projective line with itself is the sum of the two coordinate divisors, so by compatibility of the cycle class map with pullbacks and its additivity the class of the diagonal is the sum of the two pure tensors given by the class of the point and the unit in either order.

Bound the cohomology (proof lines 2913-2921): by the diagonal lemma the class of the diagonal cannot be written as a sum of fewer pure tensors than the sum of the Betti numbers, so that sum is at most two.

Determine the dimensions (proof lines 2921-2929): the degree zero cohomology is nonzero by the unit lemma, and Poincare duality makes its dimension equal to the dimension in the top degree, so the cohomology is one dimensional in degrees zero and two and vanishes in all other degrees.
proof_roadmap: Write the diagonal of the product of the projective line with itself as a sum of two divisors.
Use the diagonal lemma to bound the sum of the Betti numbers by two.
Use nonvanishing in degree zero and Poincare duality to determine the dimensions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the cohomology of the projective line is one dimensional in degrees zero and two and vanishes in all other degrees (statement lines 2901-2906). The proof (proof lines 2907-2929) computes the class of the diagonal as a sum of two pure tensors, uses the diagonal lemma to bound the total dimension, and uses nonvanishing and Poincare duality to determine the two dimensions. H3: a short computation with a dimension count, written out in full.
